support: A wallet is a tool that lets you interact with your account, using your keys.
note: Wallet software exposes account balances and tools for signing transactions. Seeing a Connect button does not mean this exhibit has connected a wallet.

support: a transaction object needs to be signed using the sender's private key
note: A transaction is an authenticated request that can change chain state. This station observes public pages and cannot sign or submit transactions.

support: Blocks are batches of transactions with a hash of the previous block in the chain.
note: Blocks organise transactions into linked history. A block explorer provides a view of that history; a webpage alone is not a consensus source.

support: a program that runs on the Ethereum blockchain
note: A smart contract has code and state at an address. Reading its address or interface is distinct from invoking a state-changing function.
ERC-20 specifies a common interface for fungible tokens, including balances and transfers. Names and symbols alone do not establish a token identity.
Explorers expose network data such as blocks, addresses and transactions. Their labels and presentation are separate from the chain records they index.

support: Whole-body connectome of a segmented annelid larva
note: The published reconstruction concerns a three-day-old Platynereis dumerilii larva. Our runtime selects a visual-to-motor subset. Anatomical connectivity alone does not establish its dynamics or a learning rule.
